label: Dwarf: short, stocky, long trunk, short limbs (softened achondroplasia)
sources: Merker et al. 2018, Development of body proportions in achondroplasia (Am J Med Genet A 176:1819): adult legs ~50% and arm span ~35% shorter than average, sitting height mildly reduced - https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ajmg.a.40356
BMN 111 (vosoritide) trial statistical plans: upper-to-lower segment ratio 1.9-2.1 in achondroplasia, ~1.0 average - https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/66/NCT03197766/SAP_001.pdf
D&D 5e Player's Handbook (2014), 'Height and Weight' table: hill dwarf 3'8" + 2d4 in (1.17-1.32 m), mountain dwarf 4'0" + 2d4 in (1.27-1.42 m)

notes.generated: by scripts/derive_species.py from the realistic preset - edit its knobs, not this file
notes.stature: D&D hill and mountain dwarves, 1.17-1.42 m [documented, game rules]
notes.bmi: a human trunk's mass on short legs: a 1.3 m dwarf at 60 kg is BMI 35. Achondroplastic adults' BMI runs high for the same reason [measured]

knobs.heads: art draws dwarves at 4-4.5 heads [folklore], but with a human-sized trunk that is a 0.28-0.32 m head on a 1.3 m body - bigger than any human head. 5.0 gives 0.26 m: the large head of achondroplasia (macrocephaly [measured]) without a cartoon
knobs.trunk: sitting height only mildly reduced in achondroplasia [measured]
knobs.leg: legs 28% short (hip to ankle, against a human with the same trunk). 0.56 here reproduces achondroplasia's ~50% [measured] and an upper/lower segment ratio of 1.9; 0.72 softens it to ~1.5, inside the design's 1.3-1.6
knobs.arm: arms 22% short: achondroplasia shortens the span ~35% for legs ~50% [measured], the same 0.7 share of the legs' 28%
knobs.girth: heavy forearms, thick neck, barrel chest; a short thigh stays as thick [folklore]
knobs.lordosis_deg: exaggerated lumbar lordosis, as in achondroplasia [measured]

notes.skin: human, weathered; every human region applies
notes.ratios: fractions of the final standing stature (spine curve applied), as presets.json; tolerances are the realistic preset's scaled with the value and by 1.3
notes.proportion: not graded: the trunk (neck base - hip joint), upper/lower segment ((H - crotch) / crotch), relative sitting height (~1 - crotch) and hanging reach, with the human's beside
notes.segments: bone length factors against the pre-warp human (pre_warp); girth and widths likewise absolute. The warp solves the final factors so the measured joints land on `ratios`

hip_above_crotch.note: the human range scaled with this species' hip-to-crotch gap

pre_warp.note: H_pre = H * stature_factor (stature: the H_pre range). Outside min/max_stature, fit at the limit and scale every segment, girth and width factor by H_pre / limit (a uniform scale)

spine.note: extra bend over a human's; thoracic forward, lumbar back, spread evenly over each span

moves.notes: derive_style gives the roll from the trunk/leg ratio: more hip flexion, abduction, anterior tilt and pelvic obliquity, less knee flexion (achondroplasia gait [measured]); Froude on ~0.55 m legs gives the quick short step. No named style needed
